belief: “I have to keep this secret. Speaking up would only make everything worse.”
belief_plain: I have to keep this secret. Speaking up would only make everything worse
origins: Secrets often start as survival. Someone said telling would ruin the family, the church, or you. Or you learned that speaking made things worse. Silence can be wise when a person is not safe to tell. The lie says you must keep the secret forever, and that speaking up will only destroy everything. You are allowed to tell a safe person. You are allowed to tell only what you choose. Telling a counselor, a hotline, or the police is not betrayal. It is a way to get help. If you are not safe right now, call 911. You can also call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233. If a child is being hurt, call Childhelp at 1-800-422-4453. A counselor can help you at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do this alone, or all at once.
self: If I tell, everything will fall apart.
I would be betraying the family or the church.
Speaking up would only make it worse for me.
Good people keep this kind of thing quiet.
God wants me to protect their reputation.
replacement: I do not have to keep this secret from every safe person. I can tell a counselor or a helper, say only what I choose, and ask for protection.
